# ADR-0135: A shader source is written from Add source

<!-- @generated begin adr-status -->
> **Status:** accepted
<!-- @generated end adr-status -->

<a id="context"></a>
## Context
[ADR-0093](0093-shader-sources-from-effect-packs.md) lets an effect pack declare shader sources: a
`[[source]]` table in `effect.toml` with one or more `[[source.pass]]` passes, `width`
and `height` settings, an optional `audio` input and `scene` params a pass can read.
Until now a person could only get one by writing the pack's files by hand, or through an
agent on MCP.

The custom shader editor (#1232, #1289, #1331, #1351) writes a filter: a `custom-<n>`
pack with one `[[effect]] shader`, whose settings come from `// @param` lines in the
WGSL. #1295 asks for the same editor in Add source, for a shader source with one pass.
A source differs from a filter in four ways the editor has to say something about: its
size, whether it reads its own last frame, whether it hears audio, and whether it reads a
scene.

**Tier.** This is agent tier under [ADR-0043](0043-narrow-maintainer-tier.md) and
R-GOV-005. It adds a client feature over a pack format ADR-0093 already accepted. It
changes no protocol message, no engine data an untrusted party may read, and no public
compatibility promise.

<a id="decision"></a>
## Decision
1. **Add source lists a Shader type** under Generated, after the engine's own generated
   kinds, whenever the engine lists any kinds. Create new writes a fresh `custom-<n>` pack
   (the first `pack.list` doesn't have, as for a filter) with `pack.write`, adds a source
   of its kind `custom-<n>/shader`, places it at 1920 × 1080 and opens its Properties
   with the shader editor over it. A custom shader source already written is listed
   under Generated by its `// @name`, after Shader, and can be created again like any
   kind.
2. **The pack has one source and one pass.** `effect.toml` holds `[[source]] id =
   "shader"` and one `[[source.pass]] id = "previous"` drawing `shader.wgsl`. The editor
   writes nothing else, and opens a pack as a source when its manifest has a `[[source]]`
   table.
3. **Four annotation lines say what a filter has no need of.** They are refused in a
   filter's shader, naming the line:
   - `// @size <w>x<h>` sets the default `width` and `height` (16 to 4096 each; 1920 ×
     1080 without it).
   - `// @feedback` adds the pass's own ID to its inputs, so `previous(uv)` reads the last
     frame it drew.
   - `// @audio` sets `audio = true`, so the source has ADR-0093's `audio` and
     `audio_source` settings and `audio_band(i)` and `audio_wave(i)` read it.
   - A `// @param <id> scene "Label"` line declares a `scene` setting, with no default,
     and adds it to the pass's inputs, read as `<id>(uv)`.

   A setting may not use one of the source settings' IDs (`width`, `height`, `audio`,
   `audio_source`) or `previous`.
4. **Properties has Edit shader….** A custom shader source's Properties dialog shows an
   Edit shader… button above its settings, which opens the same editor, live-compiling as
   for a filter. Save as pack… is a filter's only: moving a source to a new kind would
   have to move every placement of it, which this doesn't decide.

<a id="consequences"></a>
## Consequences
- No protocol change: the editor uses `pack.write`, `pack.read`, `pack.list`,
  `kind.list` and `source.create`, as Add filter's Custom shader does.
- `crates/jstream-effects/src/source_tests.rs` loads and draws a copy of what the editor
  writes, so a change to the engine's pack format that would break it fails there.
- A shader source has one pass. More passes, and `common` WGSL shared between them, need
  a pack written by hand or by an agent.
- The end-to-end fake has no source packs, so the dialog's path from Shader to the
  editor is checked by the UI's unit tests and not in a browser.
